title: 'Add Filter Plan' in Smart Exposure adds a duplicate of the same filter, with different defaults from the row above it
what_happened: The node's own subtitle is 'One row per filter'. Row 1 was seeded from the sequencer defaults (L, 3 x 2.0 s). Clicking '+ Add Filter Plan' produced a second row also set to L, with 10 x 60.0 s — neither a copy of the row above nor a value the user chose, and a duplicate of an existing filter, which the 'one row per filter' contract says is impossible. Nothing warns about the duplicate.
expected: Pick the next unused filter from the profile, and copy count/duration/gain/offset/binning from the previous row (this is what NINA's Smart Exposure does). Block or warn on duplicate filters.
repro: Configure profile filters, add Smart Exposure, click '+ Add Filter Plan'.

title: Palette search ranks description matches above exact name matches: typing 'Dither' and pressing + adds Smart Exposure
what_happened: The palette filters on name OR description and keeps the original category order. 'Smart Exposure' has the description 'One row per filter; handles rotation + dither', so searching 'Dither' lists Smart Exposure first and the actual Dither node second. Building a sequence by search-then-click-the-first-result silently gave me two Smart Exposure nodes and zero Dither nodes; I only noticed by reading the accessibility tree afterwards.
expected: Exact/prefix name matches must sort above description matches.
repro: Sequencer > Nodes > type 'Dither' in Search nodes. Smart Exposure is the first result.

title: Stop Guiding fails the whole run when nothing is guiding
what_happened: A sequence [Stop Guiding, Start Guiding] with no guider connected: 'Stop Guiding failed: Failed to stop guiding: No active guider configured' and the run aborted before Start Guiding ever ran. A Stop Guiding node is normally used in an end-of-night or pre-flip block where guiding may or may not be active.
expected: Stopping something that is already stopped is a no-op success (this is what NINA and SGP do). Reserve failure for a guider that is connected and refuses to stop.

title: Selecting a node and pressing Delete does nothing; deletion requires hovering the row and hitting a 3-state hover toolbar
what_happened: I selected the Slew to Target node (its properties panel loaded, the row showed the selected outline) and pressed Delete. Nothing happened — the header still read '4 nodes'. Deletion only worked by hovering the row until an icon strip appears and clicking the trash icon, then confirming a dialog. There is a sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart in the codebase, so shortcuts exist for other actions.
expected: Delete/Backspace on a selected node should delete it (with the same confirm dialog).
repro: Select any node in the tree, press Delete.

title: Calibrator On hardcodes a 0-255 brightness scale and states it as fact
what_happened: The Calibrator On properties show a slider fixed to 0-255 with the caption '0 = off, 255 = maximum brightness'. ASCOM/Alpaca cover calibrators report their own MaxBrightness (commonly 100, 1023 or 65535); the node has no way to read it and the caption asserts a value that will be wrong for most panels. (The node itself is also unreachable at runtime — see the dome/cover finding.)
expected: Read MaxBrightness from the connected calibrator and scale the slider and caption to it; if none is connected, say the range is the device's.

title: Smart Exposure claims 'Round-robin: RGRGRG…' regardless of what filters the node actually contains
what_happened: With a single filter plan (L), the Rotate Filters switch's caption reads 'Round-robin: RGRGRG...' — naming R and G filters that are not in the node and describing a rotation that cannot happen with one row. It reads as a description of this node's behaviour rather than a generic illustration.
expected: Build the preview string from the node's own plans, e.g. 'L L L' for one row or 'L G L G L' for the configured rows.
repro: Add Smart Exposure with one filter plan > scroll Properties to Rotate Filters.

title: Target node has two different name fields ('Name' and 'Target Name') that disagree by default
what_happened: A freshly added Target node shows 'Name: Target' at the top of the properties panel and 'Target Settings > Target Name: New Target' below it. The tree row and every run log use 'New Target'; the node label uses 'Target'. Nothing on screen explains which one matters.
expected: One field. If a node-label vs astronomical-target distinction is really needed, label them 'Step label' and 'Target', and default them to the same value.

title: Pre-flight never checks whether the devices a sequence's nodes need are present
what_happened: A sequence of [Open Cover, Calibrator On] with zero cover calibrators discovered passed pre-flight as 'Ready with Warnings' — the only warning was 'No Exposures'. The run then aborted 1 s in on 'No cover calibrator (flat panel) connected'. The same held for the dome nodes. Pre-flight does check filters for Smart Exposure and structure for Target Scheduler, so the device-requirement check simply does not cover the dome/cover family.
expected: Pre-flight should map each node type to the device it needs and error when that device is absent — that is the whole point of running it before dark.
repro: Add Open Cover + Calibrator On with no cover calibrator connected > Start.

title: The validation error/warning badges in the sequence header are not clickable
what_happened: The sequence header shows chips like '9 errors / 5 warnings / 1 info'. Clicking the red error chip does nothing — no popover, no jump to the offending node, no panel. The only way to read the issues is to press Start and open the Pre-Flight dialog, which is a strange thing to have to do while editing.
expected: Clicking a badge should open the issue list (the pre-flight content already exists) and clicking an issue should select the offending node.
repro: Build a sequence with errors, click the red '1' chip next to the sequence name.
